basis: 1A (Rose daily work plan, 2026-11-05): every release lane builds on its own runner, VM, storage, queue and lifecycle controller, so one lane's failure or cleanup cannot stop another; only genuinely shared atomic steps, such as app version allocation, may be serialized across lanes. This is the committed map: the host each os-release mode runs on today, and what each lane still needs. A host is listed only with values the committed route already uses or Infra's verified readback supplies, with its evidence; nothing here is a placeholder. A host builds only when it is in service: the Frankel builder is the operating builder, and Yogi's counts once os/ota/yogi.json says builder.status ready. scripts/tests/test_lane_capacity.py derives the actual routing from os-release.yml, release-pipeline.py and the host configs and checks it against this map.
binding: Infra adds a host with verified readback (runner label carried only by that machine, VM project/zone/instance, storage root, lock path, queue, controller identity variable) and evidence. Release then moves the lane to it: the lane's host, its jobs' runs-on, a per-host queue and a lane-aware controller, in one reviewed change that this test must pass. Until then a lane with target own stays on its current host.

frankel-builder.evidence: the committed route on main: os-release.yml (runs-on of every self-hosted job, the workflow concurrency group, the controller and cleanup identity), release-pipeline.py BUILDER, frankel.json host.lockPath and storage/builder-reclaim.json root

yogi-builder.evidence: the committed Yogi route on main (#558, f7ed9e2): yogi-ota.yml runs-on, concurrency and controller identity, and os/ota/yogi.json builder (from the handoff). Its builder.status is runner-unregistered, so the route is separate but not in service.

frankel.note: Frankel keeps the existing builder once its storage is recovered. app-reuse and app-inputs-export read a Frankel attempt on this host, so they stay with Frankel.

mustang.note: Its own host also needs the retained Mustang source tree its pipeline reads.

agent.note: The build itself needs only the public SDK, the pinned ZXing jar, the staged connection inputs and esbuild. Its host coupling is the app signer (PIXEL_APP_SIGNING_* through the signer identity), the 300 GiB free-space reserve and the shared app version ledger below. It cannot leave the ledger's host until the ledger moves.

harness.note: 1E: the standalone compile harness gets capacity separate from production releases.

frankel-host-other.note: Not release lanes of the plan: retained-tree, alpha, signing, Models, Rango and Blazer work that reads this host's trees. They stay on it.

yogi.note: Its own workflow on main since #558: every self-hosted job runs on its runner, in its own queue, with its own controller and its own VM, disk and lock (os/ota/yogi.json). It builds once yogi.json builder.status is ready; until then scripts/yogi_ota.py refuses every stage. Any further Yogi stage stays inside this workflow, on this runner and queue.

appVersionLedger.store: scripts/release-allocate.py: pixel-ota releases (drafts included), this host's attempt directories and its rose-actions reservations, read and written under the host lock
appVersionLedger.note: latest-beta and app-only both allocate dev.pixel.voice versionCodes. Run on separate hosts with this store, they could choose the same version. So the ledger must first move to a store every lane can update atomically; that is the one cross-lane serialization the plan allows.
